# RPG Psykiatrisk Klinik 1 – Gødstrup

RPG Psykiatrisk Klinik 1 – Gødstrup is a psychiatric clinical unit that appears in the Danish ADHD quality database's 2024 annual report as one of the departments reporting results for adult ADHD patients [^src1][^src2][^src3]. Its most notable result concerns Indikator 9, a national quality indicator measuring whether adult ADHD patients receive psychotherapy within one year of starting treatment. Out of 77 patients at the clinic with a relevant psychotherapy assessment, none received the qualifying treatment, giving the clinic a result of 0% (confidence interval 0-5%) [^src1].

This result stands out because it is not an isolated local failure but part of a nationwide pattern documented in the report: Indikator 9 was newly implemented on 1 April 2024, and the annual report covers only patients whose treatment course began between 1 April 2024 and 31 July 2024. Across Denmark, only 1% of 786 patients met the indicator, far below the national development target of 90%, a result the steering group attributed to a systemic lack of ADHD-specific psychotherapy services in Denmark rather than to individual clinics failing their patients. The steering group decided to keep the indicator in place but to prioritize full implementation of a related measure, Indikator 8, before pushing further on Indikator 9 — meaning RPG Psykiatrisk Klinik 1 – Gødstrup's 0% score reflects a system-wide gap in treatment infrastructure documented at the same time.

The clinic also appears twice more in the report with different results tied to 246 patients: one figure shows 138 out of 246 patients (56%, confidence interval 50-62%) meeting a reported measure, and another shows 201 out of 246 patients (82%, confidence interval 76-86%) meeting a different measure [^src2][^src3]. The surrounding report sections describe two other newly introduced indicators for adult ADHD patients — Indikator 10, measuring whether a patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of treatment start (national result: 37%, regional range 14-52%, against a 90% target), and Indikator 11, measuring whether a patient is on ADHD medication within 120 days of starting a treatment pathway (with regional results ranging from 85% in Region Nordjylland to 37% in Region Hovedstaden) — though the source text does not explicitly state which of these two indicators corresponds to which of the clinic's two other reported figures.

Taken together, the entity's significance lies in illustrating, at the level of a single clinical unit, the broader national story told in the ADHD_2024.pdf report: newly introduced quality indicators for adult ADHD patients — covering psychotherapy, social support assessment, and medication timing — show substantial gaps between target and actual performance across Danish psychiatric departments in 2024.
